Requested Service: Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the CareSource Appeals Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (arthroscopic partial meniscectomy) described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-15. The notice states that the request was denied because "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I disagree with this determination and ask that it be reversed on reconsideration.

1. The specific plan criteria have not been produced, and this appeal does not quote them.

I have not been able to obtain the text of the clinical guideline that CareSource/TurningPoint Healthcare Solutions, LLC actually applied to this request. CareSource's own provider materials indicate that musculoskeletal procedures such as knee arthroscopy are reviewed by TurningPoint against TurningPoint's clinical guidelines, which are distributed only through TurningPoint's password-protected provider portal (www.myturningpoint-healthcare.com) or on direct request from TurningPoint Provider Relations. Because that document was not accessible to me in preparing this appeal, I am not quoting or paraphrasing any specific policy criterion here, and I am not asserting that any particular numbered provision was misapplied. Instead, I am responding to the stated reason for denial using the medical record, and I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that CareSource and/or TurningPoint identify and provide in writing the specific clinical guideline, policy number, and criteria relied upon to deny this request, consistent with the plan's obligation to disclose the basis for an adverse benefit determination.

2. The imaging findings, contrary to the stated reason for denial, document a specific, well-recognized surgical indication.

The MRI of the knee dated 2026-07-19 found a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, with preserved articular cartilage and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes. This is not a case of mild degenerative change without a discrete structural lesion; the imaging documents an acute, displaced, mechanically significant meniscal tear. This finding directly supports the surgical request rather than contradicting it, and I ask that the reviewer re-examine the MRI report and images in light of this specific finding.

3. The clinical picture corroborates the imaging and the need for surgery.

- Symptom duration: 14 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- Function: the patient reports locking and giving way, is unable to squat or kneel, and is limited to level walking.
- Exam: positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- These findings are consistent with a mechanically locking meniscal tear and are documented in the surgeon's clinical notes submitted with the prior authorization request.

4. Conservative treatment was attempted and failed before surgery was requested.

- Physical therapy: 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from 2026-03-27 to 2026-07-03, with 24 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Medication: NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- Injection: a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-25 provided only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- The record therefore reflects a sustained, multi-modal course of conservative management that did not resolve the patient's mechanical symptoms, prior to the request for surgery.

5. There are no medical contraindications to surgery.

The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status.

Requested action:

I ask CareSource to reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29881, based on (a) the documented displaced, locking bucket-handle medial meniscus tear on MRI, (b) the associated mechanical symptoms and positive exam findings, (c) the failure of an adequate trial of conservative therapy (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection), and (d) the absence of any documented contraindication to surgery. In the alternative, I ask that CareSource/TurningPoint provide the specific criteria used in this denial so that the record can be supplemented to address any remaining gap.

Enclosed/attached in support of this appeal:
- MRI report of the knee, 2026-07-19
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-27 to 2026-07-03, 24 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-04-25)
- Surgeon's clinical/exam notes, Dr. Marchetti
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-15 (Reference POC-C29C7CFC4D-26579)
- [Appointment of Representative form, if this appeal is being submitted by someone other than the member]

This appeal is being submitted within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, consistent with the appeal deadline stated in the notice (by 2027-02-11).

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address, phone number, and email listed above. If expedited review is warranted due to the patient's ongoing mechanical locking symptoms, please advise us of the process for requesting an expedited internal appeal.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Casey Grant
